question: When taking the pulse of an elderly patient, it is recommended that OEC technicians:
options: use electronic devices only to obtain the pulse.
repeat and document the pulse rate every 2 minutes.
divert the patient’s attention with conversation.
take the pulse on both sides and compare the two rates.

question: You are out with a group of friends in a local tavern. One of the patrons gets argumentative and will not calm down. By the time the police arrive, the patron has gotten combative and is breaking glass bottles. The police subdue the patron and have them restrained. As you watch all of this happening, which of the following situations would cause you to be concerned?
options: The patron is threatening to sue the officers for physically restraining him.
The police have restrained the patron in a prone position on the floor.
The police say they will not release the patron until he has been seen in an emergency department.
The patron is supine on the floor, with officers holding one of his hands over his head and the other at his side.

question: It is a cold, snowy Saturday afternoon, and, unfortunately, the chair lift has broken, and a lift evacuation is required. You know that there is an adaptive skier group somewhere on the lift. As you prioritize the lift evacuation, you recognize that:
options: athletes with mobility problems are at increased risk of cold-exposure injuries.
someone will need to instruct paraplegic skiers on how to detach themselves from the sit-ski so they can be lifted out for the evacuation.
a blind skier’s guide should be evacuated before the blind skier so that the guide can direct the blind skier down.
skiers with intellectual disabilities should be left to the end because they will take a long time to understand your directions.

question: For the same individual, on average, blood pressure at age 30 compared to blood pressure to age 70 will be:
options: lower.
unrelated.
the same.
higher.

question: You have been called to assist a panicked mother who is worried about her child. When you arrive, she tells you that her 4-year-old has been quiet all morning and napping while the rest of her children were skiing. While napping her child began to “shake all over” for about 30 seconds. The child is now resting quietly and has adequate respirations. Their radial pulse is strong, and their skin is very hot and moist to the touch. Based on this presentation and information, you assume that the seizure occurred secondary to:
options: hypoxia.
altered mental status.
hypoglycemia.
a fever.

question: When mechanically restraining a patient, you should:
options: speak as harshly as necessary to get the patient to cooperate.
tell the patient you will release the restraints as soon as they calm down.
use a prone position when possible to ensure an open airway.
use a method consistent with your local protocols.

question: Family members tell you that three hours ago, their 76-year-old parent suddenly became confused and had great difficulty speaking. However, within 15 minutes, they returned to normal. Based on this description, an OEC technician should be suspicious of:
options: Alzheimer's disease.
dementia.
a stroke.
a transient ischemic attack.

question: You are teaching a class on adaptive athletes and are asked to discuss Asperger syndrome. Which of the following statements is an appropriate response?
options: “Asperger syndrome is a condition manifested by a standard group of symptoms, including physical impairments.”
“Individuals with Asperger syndrome are less likely to come in contact with rescuers than are members of the general population.”
“Asperger syndrome is an autism spectrum disorder in which the person may be fearful in unfamiliar environments.”
“Asperger syndrome implies that the person has no difficulty participating in normal day-to-day activities but may have difficulty with long-range planning.”

question: Which of the following patients is exhibiting signs of psychosis?
options: An 18-year-old who is so anxious about peer pressure that their are unable to go to school
A 37-year-old who is having hallucinations
A 72-year-old who was recently diagnosed with dementia
A recently divorced 35-year-old who sleeps most of the day and is losing weight

question: You are caring for a hearing-impaired athlete and realize that in order to communicate, you:
options: can usually speak loudly enough to be understood.
must know sign language or call for someone who does.
will need paper and a pen because most hearing-impaired individuals cannot speak.
should face the person because most hearing-impaired individuals can read lips.

question: Two of the most common medical causes of abnormal behavior are:
options: hypotension and hyperthermia.
hypoxia and hypoglycemia.
exercise and hypoglycemia.
carbon monoxide poisoning and acute myocardial infarction.

question: A 9-month-old has been stung on their tongue after sucking on a bottle that had a bee on the nipple. In comparison to the same injury in an adult, why would an OEC technician be more concerned over this child?
options: A child’s airway has more blood vessels than an adult’s, making bleeding more of a concern.
A child’s tongue is proportionally larger, increasing the chances of airway occlusion from even minor swelling.
Children tend to be highly allergic to bee stings, whereas the same allergy in adults is rare.
When injured, a child’s mouth produces more saliva, making choking a major concern.

question: The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends the use of the Pediatric Triangle to quickly determine if a child is “sick or not sick.” This method allows rescuers to quickly assess all of the following about the patient except their:
options: circulation.
breathing.
appearance.
history of illness or injury.

question: Which of the following statements shows that an OEC technician has an accurate understanding of vital signs in relation to geriatric patients?
options: "There is no difference between the vital signs of a geriatric patient and those of a young adult."
“Respiratory capacity is greatly reduced in geriatric patients."
"Fever tends to be more common and more severe in elderly patients."
"The typical resting heart rate in geriatric patients is less than 60 beats per minute."

question: A condition in which a person exhibits abnormal behavior but is able to function within the normal boundaries of reality is known as:
options: a psychosis.
a mood adjustment or affective disorder.
a behavioral emergency.
Schizophrenia.

question: An adolescent is defined as someone who is:
options: 8–16 years old.
13–18 years old.
10–16 years old.
9–18years old.

question: When caring for a patient with dyslexia, it is important to remember that:
options: you should not expect any impairment in communication.
all individuals with dyslexia have below-normal intelligence.
many dyslexic people have spasticity.
the patient may have difficulty processing new information.

question: When caring for patients with life-long intellectual disabilities:
options: use a stern, unemotional tone of voice because they may not pay attention to you.
talk to the patient as if they were at a sixth-grade level.
provide care quickly because they will not know they are cold.
include their caretakers in the assessment because they can help with communication.

question: An OEC technician asks you why you should not overextend the airway when performing a head tilt-chin lift maneuver on a pediatric patient. Which of the following replies would you make?
options: “The tongue of a pediatric patient is proportionally larger and blocks the airway when the neck is hyperextended.”
“The pediatric cervical spine is delicate and can be injured if the neck is hyperextended.”
“The esophagus in a pediatric patient is very thick and will occlude the airway if the neck is hyperextended.”
“The cartilage of the trachea is very soft and can compress if the neck is extended too far.”

question: Which of the following conditions must OEC technicians consider when evaluating hypotensive geriatric patients with altered mental status who show no signs of external bleeding, chest injury, or abdominal trauma?
options: A tib/fib fracture
A genetic hypotensive condition
A hip or pelvic fracture
Dehydration
